output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server, not from agency or new nurses. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules. These included the 15-second hold-off for brief SpO2 alarms, repeat-alarm suppression, and routing of probe-off alarms to the charge phone only. Pods A–C, on the new server, have about twice the phone notifications per nurse (79–86 per shift, up from 37–39) and doubled acknowledgement times. Pod D, still on the old server, is unchanged. Incident rates rose equally for core, agency and new-graduate nurses. Monitor alarm volume was flat, which rules out acuity and the monitor software update. Wireless coverage is not the main driver. Sick leave may be partly alarm fatigue, but a virus season is also under way, so that link is unproven. Do not approve the agency cap or performance reviews, because they would punish the wrong people. Do not switch off phone forwarding either. Restore the original rules, validated by Clinical Engineering and signed off by the alarm committee. The vendor estimate is about 4 hours plus validation. Then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Confidence is high. A quick check that notifications fall back after the restore would confirm it.
